root_cause: Yosys memory_libmap inserted emulate_read_first DFFs on AddressA/DataInA/WeA, changing the retained silicon-working OLD-mode ingress from LUT F to cycle-shifted Q. qin_pack now bypasses only structurally named emulation DFFs that directly feed a BRAM write input and share Clk0; the synthesis library advertises only rdwr old.
initialization_fix: For a narrow BRAM whose INIT_VAL contains x plus exactly one known value, qin_pack fills the physical x lanes with that value. Mixed/patterned narrow INIT layouts remain unchanged and unclaimed.
single_variable: Both images have physical INIT_VAL=1 for all 9216 bits, identical x2 dual-R/W mode, write schedule, address/control routes, clocks, and output path. They differ in eight non-CRC configuration bytes: the two DataInA source LUT truth tables store 00 versus 11.
selector_policy: both images: FCB_STAT=0x000f0002; 0 unmapped, 0 predicted, 0 legacy-abs; valid CRC; ALTA_BRAM9K X13Y4; PORTA_WIDTH=PORTB_WIDTH=01110; dual_rw=true; DataOutB lanes 1 and 2 live
consequence: A source-built open image now mutates X13Y4 x2 BRAM and the observed value follows DataInA. This qualifies the exact OLD-mode schedule/ingress composition, not arbitrary WeA polarity or gating, same-address collision behavior, byte enables, other widths/sites, independent clocks, or NEW/NO_CHANGE modes.

probe: direct hard-macro DataOutB lane read gates replacing the CACA wrapper select/delayed outputs
observed: Every image FCB-accepted. With INIT all one and requested write zero, both direct hard outputs remained one. With INIT all zero and requested write one, both direct hard outputs remained zero. The previous wrapper-visible F0/F3 pair therefore observed the synthesis emulation/delayed path rather than a mutated BRAM array.
consequence: Withdraw the exact X13Y4 x2 OLD-mode write qualification and disable automatic emulate_read_first input-DFF bypass in production Qin. Read/config/output-register/PACKEDMODE observations remain bounded as recorded. No source-built hard-BRAM write is qualified.
next_experiment: Decode the logical-to-physical x2 write ingress mapping and prove mutation through direct hard DataOut lanes before restoring any write transform or claim.

build.composition: 3 data bits (DataInA[0] SERV, DataInA[2] via X14Y4_OMUX29 SLICE9 buffer, DataInA[4] via the silicon-qualified RMUX00@(14,4)->IMUX26 ingress) written over MCU across 2 words; read back DataOutA[0],[2],[4] over the pure-wire site-read corridors. x18 INIT=0, constant ClkEn, no Port B.

observed: FCB_STAT 0x000f0002; word0 written 0b101 read 0b101, word1 written 0b010 read 0b010; matches=6/6, obs=0x15=exp; control_before and control_after both PASS; board clean.
scope: AGRV2K L48 X13Y4, x18 Port A, 3 data bits (DataInA[0],[2],[4] -> DataOutA[0],[2],[4]), 2 words, constant ClkEn, no Port B. Extends the 2-bit writable (W2E) to 3 bits by characterizing DataInA[4] ingress. Writable data WIDTH is bounded by the number of characterized DataIn ingress lanes (independent RMUX feeders exist for DataInA[0]/[1]/[4]/[10]; DataInA[2] via OMUX29), NOT by width mode. Not release-strict.

build.composition: Two W2E x18 INIT=1 arms differing ONLY in routed ByteEnA (buffers pinned so ByteEn routes the characterized corridor: be1 X14Y4_SLICE11.F->OMUX35->RMUX60->TMUX10->KMUX02 = ByteEnA[1]; be0 X14Y4_SLICE5.F->OMUX17->RMUX24->TMUX04->KMUX01 = ByteEnA[0]). Images provably distinct (be10 196446ae vs be01 6150c180, 63 bytes).

observed: be01 (low byte enabled): obs=0xe4, per-addr = W(a)=a&3. be10 (low byte routed 'protected'): obs=0xe4 IDENTICAL -- writing 0 to bits 0,2 STILL cleared them. control_before and control_after PASS both arms. The routed ByteEnA value has NO effect on the write on silicon.
consequence: ByteEn byte-lane masking is non-functional via the achievable open-flow corridor (either the array ignores ByteEn, or a routed-LOW ByteEn pin does not deliver against the unselected-HIGH default). Confirms the vendor X18_VENDOR_BYTEEN_TRUTH cube's behavior_claimed=false. Therefore native narrow-mode PACKING writes (multiple sub-words per 18-bit row, which need byte/sub-word masking to spare neighbors) are NOT achievable in the open flow. Narrow-WIDTH memories <=512 words remain writable by x18 mapping (one word per row, no masking needed).
scope: AGRV2K L48 X13Y4, x18 Port A. Controlled single-variable (ByteEnA) board comparison.

build.composition: x18 INIT=all-1, ByteEnA=2'b01 (low byte only); write W(a)=a&3 (bit1=low byte, bit14=high byte) to 8 words; read DataOutA[1] and DataOutA[14].

observed: control_before/after PASS. DataOutA[1] (low byte) = commanded d0 for all 8 words (written). DataOutA[14] (high byte) = 1 for ALL 8 words including words 0,1,4,5 where d1 was commanded 0 -> the high-byte write was BLOCKED by ByteEnA[1]=0 (held at INIT-1). vbram with ByteEnA=2'b11 had bit14 follow the command, so the lane tracks writes -> the difference is purely ByteEn.
consequence: WITHDRAW the consequence of bram-byteen-behavior-refuted-20260915. ByteEn per-byte write masking IS functional on silicon (vendor flow proves it). The earlier AGaMEMnon open-flow result (routed ByteEnA=10 vs =01 wrote identically) was an AGaMEMnon ROUTING/DELIVERY failure of the chosen ByteEn corridor (SLICE->OMUX->RMUX60/24->TMUX10/04->KMUX02/01 did not deliver the value on silicon), NOT a silicon impossibility. Native narrow-mode packing writes ARE achievable; the AGaMEMnon gap is to replicate the vendor's conducting ByteEn routing. Correcting a confidently-wrong prior conclusion out loud.
scope: AGRV2K L48 X13Y4, x18 Port A, vendor-flow ByteEn behavior confirmation. Vendor artifacts and board record live in AG32-Docs/tools/vendor_parity/bram_vendor_byteen_20260915/.

AGaMEMnon's remaining gap is purely open-flow routing of the BRAM write pins (all 18 DataInA lanes + ByteEn config + address protocol) the way the vendor routes them over the full conducting graph. vfull2.bin/bytee.bin are the byte-exact corridor sources.

observed: control_before/after PASS. ctrl arm (ByteEn default = both bytes enabled): obs=0xE4, matches=4/4, per-word obw tracks W (0,1,2,3). be0 arm (CFG_KMUX sel17 asserted): obs=0xFF, matches=1, b0m=2, b2m=2, per-word obw=3,3,3,3 (both low-byte read bits stuck at INIT-1 = writes masked). Single config-bit delta with shared firmware; ctrl proves the write path works.
consequence: Both ByteEn config bits are now board-proven: CFG_KMUX sel26 = ByteEnA[1]->gnd (high byte, vendor), CFG_KMUX sel17 = ByteEnA[0]->gnd (low byte, open flow). Per-byte write masking is a CFG_KMUX local-gnd tie (position 8 of each 9-selector lane), NOT a routed net. Unblocks native narrow-mode (x1/x2/x4/x9) write masking; native emission is a scoped routing-emitter change, not yet shipped and pending its own board qualification.
